improvements: Hand and Beetle challenges require actual walking/jumping, a grounded landing and a held pose; they no longer teleport the player to a target.
Two posed visitors moved to adjacent sculpture surfaces to clear the playable hand and Beetle targets, preserving visitor counts.
Source buildings and bridge-context geometry retain exact polygons and shared roof profiles.

Independent native pedestrian-aware travel reaches the exact public reading goal while preserving every source record, collider and visitor; the original failed static-planner attempt is retained as a separate diagnostic.
remainingGaps: The shared static route ignores moving pedestrians and can stop against a visitor. A separate pedestrian-aware native walk reaches the exact reading point; no scene geometry or crowd placement was changed. The visitor beside the plaque remains visible.
A complete matched under-bridge comparison is still missing. The available Street View sample was on the bridge deck and was rejected as unsuitable.
Touch buttons were exercised, but the climb movement in that harness still used keyboard input; a complete touch-joystick climb remains unverified.
The sculpture, Beetle and bridge materials still need an independent whole-scene comparison, including retaining walls and hillside paths.
Raw audit findings remain for physical review: zfight 72.

checks.label: High scene budgets
checks.details: 253228 unique geometry triangles; max 626276 rendered triangles / 211 calls across captured views and the native endpoint. Software GL is not a hardware frame-rate benchmark.

checks.label: Full matched scene comparison
checks.details: OSM geometry and public reference links are recorded. Complete, matched, independent scene/entry/access comparisons remain open; a model study does not establish scene parity.

checks.label: Participatory activity controls
checks.details: Native walk/jump/grounded-pose completion, no early award and cancellation pass in the activity harness; both UI sizes have 44px controls. Touch joystick movement is explicitly not proven.
